name: Combinatorial Eluder Dimension of the Triangular-Code Family
proof: Anchor at the all-zero word. Query coordinates 1,...,N in that order and use h_i as the witness at coordinate i. Its diagonal bit is one and its earlier bits are all zero, so this is an eluder sequence of length N=2^n. Coordinates cannot repeat in an eluder sequence, because a later witness must agree with the anchor at each earlier coordinate. Thus the N-coordinate domain gives the matching upper bound.
references: Direct diagonal sequence; admissibility and existence are proved in survey prop:triangular-code-range.
